project: Project Intersection / MER-EI / RVD prior art
verification_policy: Publisher/author/peer-reviewed originals preferred; where unavailable bibliographic databases and source abstract only. Distinguish public replication materials from independently rerun code or studies.
critical_inferences: RVD's VC is stricter than raising B welfare or A's prosocial output because B may have real but unused choice rights.
Own autonomy value does not imply preserving the other's choice rights; important rival mechanism.
Delegation can be voluntary and economically rational; avoid equating every delegation with subjugation.
Exit viability depends on both A and B outside options and can enable defection-and-run in repeated games.
Human lab-game and model/simulation results do not prove future AI motivational continuity or original-agent identity.

Carlsson et al. report majority coercive minimum donations in one setup, whereas Ackfeld/Ockenfels find only a minority ban the selfish option in a different charitable setup; heterogeneity and design differences bar a universal prosocial-coercion rate.

Gangadharan et al. 2018 report warm-glow donor types less paternalistic than altruistic donor types in specific donation-control tasks; welfare care and preserving beneficiary autonomy must be separately measured.
Freundt/Herz/Kopp 2026 shows heterogeneous intrinsic preference for OWN decision rights, not direct evidence of protecting an ORIGINAL OTHER B's freedom.
prior_overlap: Bartling, Fehr and Herz (2014) already cited in RVD earlier cycle and not recounted as new source in this incremental ledger. Chlass working-paper and final article are versions of one scholarly lineage; Ambuehl openICPSR dataset is a replication PACKAGE, not a replication STUDY. Freundt/Herz/Kopp CESifo 2023 working paper and 2026 JPubE journal article are one underlying lineage, not independent replications.
unreviewed_gaps: Choice of original B versus a replacement with the same welfare/competence
Actor A values B's veto even when idealized beneficiary result worse
A may lose exploit-option profits while preserving B's refusal
Ability to revoke voluntary delegation and real continuity after exit
Heterogeneous action-cost shape and distribution under power reversal
Longitudinal preference stability without measurement-induced motivational changes

studies.authors: Sandro Ambuehl; B. Douglas Bernheim; Axel Ockenfels
studies.title: What Motivates Paternalism? An Experimental Study
studies.mechanism: ideal-projective paternalism despite alternatives including advice
studies.rival_to: welfare-or-helpful-intention implies beneficiary independent choice rights
studies.interpretation: Helping intentions can coincide with denying chooser options; not proven exploitation or long-run rights outcome.
studies.scope: AER publisher abstract, author webpage; full text not audited

studies.authors: Fredrik Carlsson; Mitesh Kataria; Elina Lampi; Maria Vittoria Levati
studies.title: Doing good with other people's money: An experiment on people's (UN) willingness to grant others the freedom to choose
studies.mechanism: allocators setting positive minimum contribution limits others' choice for environmental charity
studies.rival_to: prosocial environmental goals imply beneficiary's unrestricted autonomy
studies.interpretation: Majority in this sample restricted freedom, but not a universal percentage across populations.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract and article excerpt; full text not audited

studies.authors: Nadine Chlass; Werner Güth; Topi Miettinen
studies.title: Purely procedural preferences — Beyond procedural equity and reciprocity
studies.mechanism: preferences across procedures with matched expected outcomes, intentions and material payoff model predictions
studies.interpretation: May involve simplicity, efficiency and rights; cannot isolate other-regarding autonomy solely from procedure preference.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract and extended excerpt; 2009 working paper is an edition of related work, not additional independent confirmation

studies.authors: João V. Ferreira; Nobuyuki Hanaki; Benoît Tarroux
studies.title: On the roots of the intrinsic value of decision rights: Experimental evidence
studies.mechanism: self-reliance rather than power or independence was statistically important rationale for holding one's own decision rights in the reported treatments
studies.rival_to: intrinsic self-control equals intrinsic respect for another's independent control
studies.interpretation: Self autonomy is distinct from respecting original B's choice; cross-country treatments not AI.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract and introduction; full text not audited

studies.authors: Seda Ertac; Mert Gumren; Mehmet Y. Gurdal
studies.title: Demand for decision autonomy and the desire to avoid responsibility in risky environments: Experimental evidence
studies.mechanism: valuing own decision right vs avoiding responsibility to decide for others differ
studies.rival_to: more control or power always desirable, delegation always signals reduced freedom
studies.interpretation: Preference to delegate can reflect burden, risk and responsibility; voluntary delegation must remain revocable to test ongoing choice.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract and introduction; full text not audited

studies.title: At-will relationships: How an option to walk away affects cooperation and efficiency
studies.mechanism: outcome of outside-option and exit opportunity depends on asymmetric division and partner opportunities
studies.rival_to: an exit button always increases both sides' welfare or cooperation
studies.interpretation: Need distinct actual outside-option value for A and B; average cooperation insufficient.
studies.scope: RePEc publisher bibliographic extraction and abstract; full text not audited

studies.title: Mutualism, market effects and partner control
studies.mechanism: vulnerable actor's partner termination leverage depends on both players' ability to find new partners
studies.rival_to: formal leave permission always provides effective deterrence
studies.interpretation: Partner scarcity and exploiter replacement ease can make the vulnerable partner's exit ineffective.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract only; not an experiment on AI.

studies.authors: Christopher Graser; Takako Fujiwara-Greve; Julián García; Matthijs van Veelen
studies.title: Repeated games with partner choice
studies.mechanism: partner choice can elevate evolved cooperation but can permit exploit-then-leave strategies under model-specific conditions
studies.rival_to: leaving unambiguously eliminates exploitation or creates unconditional high cooperation
studies.interpretation: Beneficial population average and defection-run edge cases coexist; no direct observational agent experiment.
studies.scope: Open-access original full paper abstract/introduction and relevant theorem-context discussion reviewed; no code executed

studies.authors: Randolph Sloof; Ferdinand A. von Siemens
studies.title: Illusion of control and the pursuit of authority
studies.mechanism: willingness to pay for authority even when decision power gives no objective information advantage
studies.rival_to: A's desire for control can be read directly as objective instrumental payoff benefit
studies.interpretation: Own authority-seeking not a proof of treating other B as intrinsically valuable.
studies.scope: Publisher abstract only; version/publication date independently confirm if used for quant results

studies.authors: Holly Dykstra; Christine Exley; Muriel Niederle; Heather Wong
studies.title: When Decisions Require Consideration, People Give Up Control
studies.mechanism: cognitive consideration cost can increase willingness to delegate own agency
studies.rival_to: delegation automatically indicates low intrinsic valuation of control
studies.interpretation: Working paper; do not count as published journal replication.
studies.scope: CEPR original working paper abstract, January 9 2026

studies.authors: Lata Gangadharan; Philip J. Grossman; Kristy Jones; C. Matthew Leister
studies.title: Paternalistic giving: Restricting recipient choice
studies.mechanism: warm-glow-oriented donors were significantly less paternalistic than altruistic donors in these cash-vs-in-kind donation tasks
studies.rival_to: pure concern for other's welfare always preserves other's choice while warm glow generates more control
studies.interpretation: Context-specific donor types and perceptions; measured type depends on authors' elicitation assumptions, not a proof of universal motive distribution or future AI.
studies.scope: Original university/publisher abstract and article excerpt; full text not independently audited

studies.title: Do people intervene to make others behave prosocially?
studies.mechanism: only a minority of self-donors ban recipient's selfish option; intervention acceptance depends on respecting autonomous choice sequence
studies.rival_to: all prosocial agents readily coerce other agents or majority intervention generalizes across different task incentives
studies.interpretation: Direct contrast with Carlsson 2017 study under different designs and choice contexts, NOT a simple failed replication of the same task.
studies.scope: Publisher original abstract and author institutional record; full text not audited

studies.authors: Jana Freundt; Holger Herz; Leander Kopp
studies.title: Choosing (not) to choose: Uncovering intrinsic preferences for choice autonomy
studies.mechanism: study reports intrinsic valuation of one's own choice autonomy and a substantial minority that prefers not to choose, controlling instrumental choice gains within their elicitation model
studies.rival_to: all rational or moral agents intrinsically prefer maximum self-autonomy and therefore protect other's autonomy
studies.interpretation: Own agency, not preference to protect the other B; randomized choice and model assumptions matter. Same scholarly work as 2023 CESifo working paper, not second study.
studies.scope: Elsevier publisher abstract and university author publication listing; full text not independently audited
